summary: Report safe failure locations in the adoption-lock fixture

delivery.outcome: Make an unexpected adoption-lock fixture failure report a bounded numeric source line and the original nonzero exit status before existing cleanup.
nonGoals: Do not claim the previous hosted CI root cause is established
No production installer, consumer adoption, version, release or runtime dependency changes
Do not remove assertions, accept more errors, change timeouts or print environment/fixture contents

architecture.decision: Keep the existing errexit/pipefail and cleanup traps. Add an inherited ERR handler to the single Bash fixture. It emits only a fixed label, failing line and original status, then exits with that status. Conditional expected failures remain guarded as before.
architecture.rollback: Reviewed revert of the diagnostic handler; original test assertions and cleanup remain intact.

validation.evidence: The full existing script succeeds without failure output. Bounded external fault-injection copies exercise top-level and function failures, verify original statuses, numeric line diagnostics and cleanup, with no secret/environment output.
Native hub checks/full Python suite, protected exact-head Linux/Windows/OneDev and independent review precede merge.
